tool_usage.tool_name: GitHub Copilot coding agent (CCA) in dotnet/runtime
what_for: Assigning GitHub issues to Copilot, which plans the work, opens a PR, writes code, and runs tests
Code maintenance, modernization, and large-scale refactors
Fixing bugs and improving CI/CD pipeline stability
Automatic AI-powered code review on every PR in the repo (human-, CCA-, and external-authored)
tool_usage.teams: .NET team (dotnet/runtime open-source repository: .NET runtime, GC, JIT, AOT toolchain, core libraries; C#/C++/assembly)
tool_usage.scale: 878 CCA pull requests over ~10 months, 535 merged, 67.9% success rate; experiment began the day CCA launched publicly (May 2025). Figures from Microsoft's own .NET blog (primary, single post).
tool_usage.confidence_note: High confidence; primary Microsoft devblog with explicit quantified outcomes, though numbers come from a single self-reported post.

tool_usage.tool_name: GitHub Copilot coding agent in github.com core repository
what_for: Human engineers assign issues to @Copilot, which opens PRs and completes the work
Tedious/repetitive tasks: fixing 161 typos across 100 files in one PR
Removing deprecated feature flags; cleaning up conditional logic, stale code, and old tests
Patching production bugs and improving CI/CD pipeline stability (e.g., NoMethodError fixes, caching error-masking fixes)
tool_usage.teams: GitHub engineering (core repository used to build github.com)
tool_usage.scale: Based on analysis of one month of Copilot-authored PRs in GitHub's core repo; described qualitatively as 'a prolific engineer.' No headcount/seat or percentage figure published in the post.
tool_usage.confidence_note: High confidence on tasks/use cases (primary GitHub blog, Nov 12 2025); scale is qualitative rather than a hard number.

what_for: Agentic command-line coding workflows (long-running sessions iterating through tests, files, and commands)
Becoming Microsoft's single internal agentic CLI, replacing Claude Code
tool_usage.teams: Experiences + Devices org (engineers on Windows, M365, Teams, Outlook, Surface)
tool_usage.scale: Reporting describes 'thousands of engineers' being moved off Claude Code onto Copilot CLI with a June 30, 2026 deadline. Figure is from journalism citing internal communications; treat as approximate.
tool_usage.confidence_note: Medium-high; multiple credible outlets plus Pragmatic Engineer corroborate, but scale/teams rely on internal-memo reporting, not an official Microsoft statement.

tool_usage.tool_name: Anthropic Claude Code (being phased out internally)
what_for: Agentic CLI-based software development by Microsoft engineers (reportedly the more popular internal tool before the mandated switch)
tool_usage.teams: Experiences + Devices org (Windows, M365, Teams, Outlook, Surface)
tool_usage.scale: Widely adopted internally per reporting; most internal licenses being canceled by June 30, 2026. No exact seat count published.
tool_usage.confidence_note: Medium; existence and popularity of internal Claude Code use is reported by multiple outlets, but precise scale is unquantified and based on internal-memo journalism.

tool_usage.tool_name: Anthropic Claude models in Copilot Studio / Foundry / GitHub Copilot
what_for: Selectable models for building, orchestrating, and managing agents in Copilot Studio (advanced reasoning, workflow automation)
Claude Sonnet 4 / Opus 4.1 in Copilot Studio; Claude Opus 4.6 in Foundry and rolling out across GitHub Copilot
tool_usage.teams: Microsoft Copilot / Copilot Studio / Foundry product teams (customer-facing offering)
tool_usage.scale: Available by default in most geographies as of Jan 6, 2026 (EU/UK/EFTA require admin opt-in). Customer-facing, not an internal-headcount metric.
tool_usage.confidence_note: High confidence; primary Microsoft Copilot blog plus corroborating coverage. This is product integration, not internal dev usage.

notes: Best HOW/WHAT-FOR detail comes from two primary dogfooding sources: dotnet/runtime (878 PRs, 535 merged, 67.9% success; refactors, bug fixes, AI code review on every PR) and the github.com core repo (typo cleanups, feature-flag removal, schema migrations, CI/CD and production bug patches). Internal Copilot CLI standardization and the Claude Code phase-out (Experiences + Devices, June 30 2026) are well-reported but scale figures ('thousands of engineers') come from internal-memo journalism, not official Microsoft data, so they are caveated. Anthropic-model availability inside Copilot/Studio/Foundry is product integration, distinct from internal dev usage. Microsoft is also the vendor/maker of all GitHub Copilot capabilities. No credible evidence of internal Microsoft standardization on Cursor, Windsurf, or Devin was found.
